themes_detail.label: Food Poisoning Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Nine food poisoning complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. a baseline of 2.1 per week (up 324%), representing a statistically significant spike (z-score: 6.53) that suggests a potential foodborne illness outbreak or restaurant hygiene problem in the district this week or last.
evidence: 9 food poisoning complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 2.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.53)
324% increase above baseline is among the highest-magnitude spikes in the dataset
Greenwich Village/SoHo has dense restaurant concentration; outbreak could affect hundreds
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Health to identify which restaurants triggered complaints and whether inspections found violations
Interview residents who filed complaints about symptoms, timing, and which establishments they patronized
Investigate whether a specific restaurant or food supplier is linked to multiple cases

themes_detail.label: Elevator System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Nine elevator complaints filed last week vs. a baseline of 2.0 per week (up 350%, z-score: 6.26), indicating a potential surge in building maintenance failures or system degradation across residential and commercial properties in the district.
evidence: 9 elevator complaints last week vs. 2.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.26)
350% spike is the second-highest magnitude increase in the dataset
SoHo and Greenwich Village have many converted loft buildings and older residential structures with aging elevator infrastructure
reporting_angles: Request DOB data on recent elevator inspection failures and violations in CD 102
Interview building managers about staffing, maintenance schedules, and budget constraints affecting elevator upkeep
Investigate whether the spike correlates with a specific weather event, power outage, or seasonal maintenance pattern

themes_detail.label: Street Tree Damage Surge
themes_detail.summary: Eight complaints about dead/dying trees and illegal tree damage filed last week combined (3 dead tree + 5 illegal damage complaints vs. baselines of 0.4 and 0.9 respectively), totaling a 586% aggregate spike and indicating possible environmental stressors, storms, or illicit cutting in the district.
evidence: Dead/Dying Tree: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.4 average (z-score: 5.42, up 700%)
Illegal Tree Damage: 5 complaints last week vs. 0.9 average (z-score: 5.28, up 471%)
Community Board budget requests repeatedly cite need for forestry services and street tree maintenance (unfunded/ongoing problem)
Combined signal suggests environmental or maintenance crisis
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Parks Department to determine if recent weather, pests, or disease is causing tree die-off across the district
Investigate whether construction activity (1,642 DOB permits filed in 90 days, including 1,429 alterations) is damaging tree root systems or canopy
Interview residents and local gardeners about observed tree conditions and potential illegal pruning or removal

themes_detail.label: Water Quality Contamination Alert
themes_detail.summary: Four water quality complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. a baseline of 0.4 per week (up 967%, z-score: 5.21), suggesting possible contamination, taste/odor issues, or supply problems affecting neighborhood residents and businesses.
evidence: 4 water quality complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.21, up 967%)
Among highest-magnitude spikes in dataset; represents acute public health concern
Community Board budget requests include 'Clean catch basins' (DEP), suggesting ongoing water infrastructure vulnerability
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection to confirm whether contamination, main breaks, or boil-water advisories affected the district
Interview 311 complainants about water discoloration, odor, taste, or supply interruptions and cross-reference with service areas
Check whether recent construction or utility work disrupted water mains or pressure in the area

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Sixty-five commercial noise complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. a baseline of 39.5 per week (up 65%, z-score: 3.55), indicating sustained operational noise issues from restaurants, bars, music venues, or construction in this densely commercial district.
evidence: 65 noise-commercial complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 39.5 weekly average (z-score: 3.55, up 65%)
Commercial noise complaints rank 7th in overall 90-day volume (539 total), indicating endemic issue
May correlate with post-election policy shifts under new Council Member Carl Wilson or seasonal reopenings
reporting_angles: Identify which business types (bars, music venues, restaurants, construction) are driving the spike via 311 complaint details
Interview residential neighbors adjacent to commercial areas about noise timing and sources
Check whether recent nightlife or restaurant openings or construction permits correlate with complaint surge
